title: Lab: price a ring all-reduce
summary: Estimate gradient synchronisation time with the bandwidth and latency terms of ring all-reduce.

blocks.md: In data-parallel training every worker must end each step with the sum of all gradients. A ring all-reduce does it in $2(N-1)$ rounds; in each round every worker sends $1/N$ of the data to its neighbour. Each worker therefore sends $2\frac{N-1}{N}S$ bytes in total, which is why the time barely depends on $N$ but never drops below $2S/BW$.

blocks.title: 7B model, bf16 gradients (14 GB), 64 workers, 50 GB/s links, 5 µs per round

steps.why: The bytes every worker must push through its link.
One fixed start-up cost per round.
Bandwidth-bound: the latency term is a rounding error at this message size.

challenge.md: Keep 14 GB and 50 GB/s but use only **8 workers**. What is the all-reduce time in seconds?
challenge.explanation: 2 × 0.875 × 0.28 = 0.49 s (+0.07 ms latency). Going from 8 to 64 workers adds only 12%: the ring scales.

blocks.title: All-reduce cost model
blocks.md: Complete `ring_allreduce_s(size_gb, n, bw_gbs, alpha_us)` returning seconds, then print it for 8, 64 and 1,024 workers. Notice when the latency term starts to matter.
blocks.check:
assert abs(ring_allreduce_s(14, 64, 50, 5) - (2 * 63 / 64 * 14 / 50 + 2 * 63 * 5e-6)) < 1e-9
assert abs(ring_allreduce_s(14, 8, 50, 0) - 0.49) < 1e-9
assert ring_allreduce_s(0.001, 1024, 50, 5) > 0.01, 'small messages on many workers are latency-bound'

questions.q: How many bytes does each worker send in a ring all-reduce of 14 GB across 64 workers (GB, 2 decimals)?
questions.explanation: 2 × 63/64 × 14 = 27.56 GB: about twice the gradient, whatever N is.

questions.q: A 1 MB gradient bucket is all-reduced across 1,024 workers. What dominates?
questions.explanation: 2 × 1023 rounds × 5 µs ≈ 10 ms of latency against about 0.04 ms of transfer. Tree or hierarchical algorithms and larger buckets fix this.

points: The bandwidth term is nearly independent of N; the latency term grows with N.
Large buckets keep it bandwidth-bound; hierarchy helps at very large N.
